section_summaries.summary: The guideline is scoped to authorized insurers underwriting long term business other than Class C business, and compliance assessment focuses on substance over the label of an arrangement.

Product governance should consider fair treatment from design through post-launch monitoring, including target customers, affordability, risk profile, distribution channel, fees, charges, and surrender effects.
Customer-facing materials should be understandable and should cover material risks, exclusions, fees, charges, surrender consequences, and cooling-off rights before the customer commits.

section_summaries.citation: HKIA GL16/GN16 section 7 and Annex sales process
section_summaries.summary: Before advice or sale, records should show a needs and suitability review that considers customer knowledge, experience, priorities, circumstances, affordability, and premium payment horizon where relevant.
Intermediary remuneration should avoid misaligned incentives, should not permit indemnity or advance commission, and should include clawback for proven fraud, money laundering, or mis-selling.
Controls should manage conflicts of interest and maintain policyholder communication, including expectation management for non-guaranteed or illustrated benefits.
Where policy loan features exist, customer information should cover loan terms, interest rates, notices, rate changes, balances, and account statement controls.

Vulnerable-customer controls should identify applicable customers, run audio-recorded post-sale confirmation calls, handle unsuccessful calls with follow-up notices, and retain quality-control records.

non_authoritative_notice: This corpus is for deterministic Layer-1 triage. It is not legal advice and is not an HKIA submission artifact.
